Introduction
Evolution of the Lands
Parkview Cemetery and Bechtel Park have evolved, gradually, since the mid 1950’s,
when the lands were a combination of wood land, creek valley corridor and farmland at
the edge of the city. The land parcel was acquired from Mr. Levy Bechtel and has
served the community well, as both a community cemetery, and a major community
park.
The cemetery was originally planned for the ent ire 74 acre parcel of developable land.
Today the cemetery is 26 acres in size and is nearing capacity for traditional casket
burial lots. In the mid 1970’s part of th e lands were planned and established as
parkland with sports facilities which are co nsidered to be ‘premium’ sport venues in
Waterloo.
All planning decisions over the last 30 plus years, were to best se rve the citizens of
Waterloo with a community cemetery, natur al environment, and parklands with an array
of recreational opportunities.
Parkview Cemetery is currently faced wit h an immediate land shortage for traditional
casket interment lots. Bechtel Park is a community park with year round active and
passive facilities for which the last Master Plan was prepared in 1991. Although the
cemetery and the park share the lands, a combined Master Plan has never been
undertaken.
The purpose of the Cemetery Services – Bechtel Park Master Pl an is to provide a
comprehensive land-use and deli very of service guide for the Parkview Cemetery and
Bechtel Park lands. The Master Plan will address land-use development and
operational strategies based on the following objectives.
 To address cemetery pressures.
 To analyze long-term cemetery needs.
 To analyze long-term park needs.
 To assess the inventory of sports fields and facilities in the park.
 To plan an approach for delivering cemetery services.
 To plan for improvements to the cemetery and park.
 To evaluate the preservation and protection of the sensitive environmental features.
Key Strategic Elements of the Master Plan
This Master Plan establishes a vision for the lands as a whole, including cemetery
spaces, natural spaces and activity spaces. The plan fulfills an effort to balance needs
by integrating the activities that are curr ently firmly rooted on the lands. The Master
Plan also establishes an appr oach to service delivery for Waterloo Cemeteries as a
Self-Funded Enterprise Model.
1

Vision for the Lands as a Whole:
The lands will continue to serve the community with three primary functions.
1) nature appreciati on and learning,
2) remembrance, contemplation and healing,
3) year-round fitness and active recreation.
Decisions to be made over the next 15 years are directed by five Policy Statements and
supporting Implementation Initiatives.
The Master Plan and the success of future of cemetery services hinges on a new or
alternative cemetery being established for the Waterloo community. It is also expected
that over the next decade recreational needs will also evolve.
An improved trail system is f undamental to the cohesive existence of all three activities.
Expanded trails will in crease pedestrian circulation and enliven the entire property with
positive recreational activity. Connectivity of the lands through the introduction of trails
will open gateways between the cemetery and parkl ands where a visit to the cemetery
may be followed by a walk through the wood s and loop through the park. Tree lined
trails will connect spaces and serve as a buffer between spaces providing different
uses.
Programmed sport will continue to be encouraged in Bechtel Park, however, to align
with the recommendations of the Recreation & Leisure Services Master Plan, the
premium (class A) outdoor sport facilities are to be relocated to the two park venues
where high-quality, premium s port fields and ball diamonds wi ll be concentrated. The
RLS Master Plan identifies RIM Park and a west-side location (not yet determined) as
the ideal venue for premium sports clusters.
Options for replacement of the two premiu m sport fields (Bechtel #5 and #6), and
consideration of a future location for a pr emium ball facility (to replace the Bechtel
Stadium), will be determined by staff in 20 09, as staff examine the broader city-wide
distribution and capacity of sport facilities. This will include consultation with the sport
stakeholder groups to meet t he needs of our own community, as well as, consideration
of opportunities to enhance sport tourism events.
It is important to note that Be chtel Park will continue to se rve as a secondary sport field
cluster for a variety of minor sport programming. The Park will also continue to serve
as a node for a diversity of passive and or ganized recreational activities. Further
improvements and enhancements that support the existing wide range of activities
including, walking, running, skiing, dog walking, access to a leash-free dog zone, nature
appreciation, bird watching and outdoor educ ation/class studies, will be considered
within the existing annual city budgets, and where possible through partnership
opportunities.
The Manulife Financial Soccer and Sports Centre will be sustained as the indoor facility
at Bechtel Park to provide year round s port opportunities. Capital upgrades will
continue to keep the facility current, as was done in late 2008 with a new artificial turf
surface which was made possibl e through partnersh ip with the Waterloo Minor Soccer
Club.
Partnership will be the cornerstone to u ndertaking major enhancements, and staff will
work to identify and build capacity for collaborative efforts to implement the Master Plan.
2

Cemeteries as Self-Funding Enterprise
Financial sustainability of Waterloo Cemeteries is a primary goal. Waterloo Cemeteries
have operated as a self-supportive operati on since 1997. The City of Waterloo
Cemetery Services model is somewhat uni que when compared to t he majority of other
municipally operated cemeteries in the Province of Ontario that typically run a deficit
and require tax roll support. Waterloo Cemete ries currently operates without tax roll
support, and also, supports a percentage of the overhead related to Bechtel Park
operations, and contributes $60,000 annually to the Corporati on in the form of General
Government Overhead.
Moving forward, for Waterloo Cemeteries to continue to operate as a self-funded
enterprise model that is independent of tax support, corporate decisions must
consistently have regard for sustaining the enterprise model.
The goal, to remain a self-funded enter prise model, will be supported through the
following strategies.
a) Annual review and consi deration of the cemetery fee structure and products &
services, implementing changes were necessary in compliance with the
Cemeteries Act.
b) Continued contributions and, thus, increases to the cemetery care &
maintenance fund principal.
In 1955 the Province of Ontario Cemeteries Act legislated the establishment of ‘Care
and Maintenance Fund’ (CMF) contributions to fund the perpetual responsibility to
maintain cemeteries.
Waterloo’s Care and Maintenance Fund was analyzed within the ‘Waterloo Cemeteries
Business Case Study’ (2006) and like most cemeteries established before 1955, the
CMF is inadequate, primar ily because historic contributions to the fund were too low or
fees for interment rights were priced too low. A significant portion of this CMF shortfall
can be attributed to Mount Hope Cemetery were the majority of sales activity took place
prior to 1955.
The Master Plan supports continued contribut ions to the Waterloo Cemeteries Care &
Maintenance Fund to move toward full realiz ed financial sustainabil ity. This will be
achieved by continuing to offer cemetery services, which benefit the community, as well
as, contributing to the CMF fund.
Next Steps
The Master Plan sets the future direction for Bechtel Park and Waterloo Cemeteries
over a 15 year period. The Master Plan triggers consideratio ns within other ongoing
and new initiatives. By nature, the plan will be an evolving process guided by the
Policy Statements, Implement ation Initiatives and Impl ementation Plan. Detailed
actions, designs, costs and funding allocations will be built into existing budgets where
possible and staff will report back to Council for approval at key milestones.
3

1.0 Strategic Direction
VISION
A ‘comprehensive’ strategy for the lands occupied by Parkview Cemetery and Bechtel
Park considering various factors including community need, environmental
sustainability, public access, and long-range land-use designations for,
 parklands,
 natural resources,
 active sports facilities,
 passive recreational pursuits, and
 cemetery and memorialization opportunities.
The master plan considers all features, functions, community needs, and the
relationships between the park, cemetery and environmental lands.
The proposed land-use plan establishes goals for achieving public parklands which are
accessible, active, safe, and attractive, with a focus on best possible use of the lands, to
serve the community. The land-use plan sustains natural landscapes, fosters
community social interaction, enhances recreational opportunities and provides for a
diversity of community cemetery and memorialization needs. The proposed plan gives
consideration to the broader, city-wide strategies, and identifies alternative options,
processes and improvements.
The master plan will include an achievable implementation process that is adaptable to
future considerations, as community needs evolve. The master plan establishes clear
goals for the ongoing long-range management of the lands, based on a need to balance
service to the community, while making the best use of a limited land base.
STUDY GOALS
 To develop a master plan and policy framework that guides decision making for the
lands shared by Bechtel Park and Parkview Cemetery.
 To develop strategic goals for the Parkview-Bechtel lands, including land-use
designations, facility and infrastructure asset management plans, capital
improvements, and operational functions.
 To provide a phasing and budgetary strategy for the recommendations of the Master
Plan.
5

GUIDING PRINCIPLES
The following principles guided the development of the master plan.
Public Access and Use of the Lands
The Master Plan will be based on optimizing opportunities for the general public to
use the lands for a variety of healthy lifestyles activities. The lands will provide for
use throughout the day to create a socially vibrant and interactive place.
Protection, Enhancement & Sustainability of the Natural Environment Resources
The Master Plan will be based on continued commitment to the health of the
woodlot, plant species, creek corridor, wildlife and bird habitat, and sensitive
ecosystems on the lands.
Enhance the Public Image and Identity of the Lands
The Master Plan will be based on integrating the lands with the surrounding urban
fabric, as a recognizable public landscape, that clearly communicates the public
options for use of the lands. The proper ty will be well maintained, aesthetically
attractive, and a safe place where people can enjoy a parkland setting.
Address Park Users Needs
The Master Plan will be based on providing passive and active recreational
opportunities that have been enjoyed by residents for over 30 years and with
consideration of provision for future recreational needs and city-wide strategies.
Address Cemetery Services Needs
The Master Plan will be based on community need for cemetery services, offering
both traditional cultural needs and other innovative (or emerging) trends/options that
will minimize land-use consumption by the cemetery.
Optimize Best Practices & Best Use of Resources
The Master Plan will be based on the best possible use of the lands, the best
possible operational practices, while remaining adaptable to change as it occurs,
including change in technology, economics, social and environmental.
Align with City of Waterloo Corporate Strategies
The Master Plan will align with the various corporate frameworks including the City
of Waterloo Strategic Plan, Official Plan, Recreation and Leisure Services Master
Plan and other linked Master Planning Processes.
6

2.0 Summary of Key Findings
Refer to ‘Cemetery Services – Bechtel Park Master Plan Appendices, Appendix D:
Inventory & Analysis’ under separate cover for a detailed review of site features,
elements and structures.
Parkview Cemetery
 Need to expand cemetery land base. There is an urgent need for additional
traditional casket interment lots and there is limited land for growth.
 Cremation services are increasing, however, demand for traditional burial lots is
steady.
 Cemetery Care & Maintenance Funds are inadequately funded. Need strategies
to ensure financial resources are available for perpetual care of properties.
 Joint-services opportunities with City of Kitchener may realize efficiencies.
 Need to amend practice/policy for long-range dedication of lands to groups.
 High maintenance landscape – need to consider opportunities to shift to lower
maintenance in new development or section amendments.
 Need to identify cemetery areas requiring capital upgrades (ie Children’s
Section).
 A variety of challenges for entering and exiting, for both vehicles and pedestrians
based on increasing volumes of traffic.
 Limited Integration with Bechtel Park.
Bechtel Park
 Limited parkland frontage. Visual exposure to community is limited.
 Entrance and exit challenges for vehicles.
 Weak parking lot layout – there is an adequate quantity of spaces.
 Lack of pedestrian facilities.
 Limited washroom facilities for the use number of park users.
 Confusing vehicular circulation.
 Road system consumes more land than needed.
 Vehicles have access to the edge of the woodlot presenting a safety and
environmental issue.
 Weak signage - upgrades are needed.
 Aging facilities and infrastructure.
 Pedestrian access to leash free zone does not function as planned.
 Playground is in poor location – safety concern and it is not linked to other
activity zones.
 Too many building structures obstructing sightlines present a safety concern.
 Lack of shade trees. A tree plan is needed. The central treed corridor should be
retained
 Seating and rest zones are needed throughout the park
 Limited daytime use of park – day activities should be encouraged
 Review potential for trail connection to City of Kitchener.
7

Recreational Facilities
 A building assessment has identified maintenance improvements that need to be
undertaken to the Manulife Financial Soccer & Sports Complex. This facility is
highly used.
 Tennis Courts are well used in the evenings. No rationale to remove at this time.
 Baseball Stadium is used moderately. There are critical structural issues.
Consider moving programming to a new location in a diamond cluster setting to
maximize programmability.
 Sport Fields are in high demand due to high quality and lighting on fields 5 and 6.
 Leash Free Zone is well used and is only facility in Waterloo. Access path is the
primary issue. Amenities are needed.
 Trails are highly used, however, wayfinding, identification and interpretive
signage is needed.
 Trail issue: most southerly section of trail is encroaching onto private lands.
Natural Resources: Woodlands, Creek Corridor, Wetlands
 Need to redefine boundary of natural areas for management purposes.
 Need to update mapping of wetland and creek zones.
 Interpretive signage to educate public on significance of the natural areas.
 Issues with Laurel Creek management south of, and outside of Bechtel Park
boundaries, but effecting creek on City lands – need to encourage good
management practices on private lands.
 Continue to protect the natural resources, habitat areas and practice
environmental stewardship.
8

3.0 Recommendations
Recommendations are divided into three categories. The following outlines the
purpose, function and use of each category. :
a) Policy Statements
The Master Plan consists of five Policy Statements. The Policy Statements provide the
strategic foundation to be adopted in all decision making for Parkview Cemetery and
Bechtel Park.
Policy Statement #1  Retain Modified Bechtel Park as a Community Park
Policy Statement #2  Provide Cemetery Services to the Community
Policy Statement #3  Operate Cemeteries as Self-Funding Enterprise
Policy Statement #4  Enhance & Integrate the Park & Cemetery
Policy Statement #5  Seek Partnerships
b) Implementation Initiatives
Each Policy Statement is supported by a series of specific ‘Implementation Initiatives’ or
actions which are essential to fully execute the master plan vision. The initiatives guide
decisions and staging of the evolution of the master plan. Each initiative will be
embedded into project planning and partnership discussions.
c) Implementation Plan
The Implementation Plan sets timeframes to initiate/achieve the most critical
implementation initiatives, particularly for decisions and actions regarding the premium
sport facilities which have an effect on other park locations, as well as, the city’s ability
to continue to provide a diversity of cemetery services in the future.
The following pages detail the Master Plan Recommendations.
9

Policy Statement #1
 Retain ‘Modified’ Bechtel Park as Community Park
The City of Waterloo will retain Bechtel Park & Woodlot as a Community Park to provide
a range of recreational opportunities for passive outdoor activities and active
programmed sport while at the same time managing an important environmental asset.
The Recreation and Leisure Services Master Plan recommends a transition of Bechtel
Park from offering ‘premium’ active sport facilities, moving toward serving as a
secondary venue. ‘Premium’ refers to sport facilities designed for the highest levels of
programmed sport. At Bechte l Park this includes sport fields #5 and #6, and the
baseball stadium.
The premium field facilities for organized sport will be established at RIM Park and/or a
proposed new site in west Waterloo. Sport Fields #5 and #6 will be relocated to allow
for lands to be converted to cemetery. The Bechte l Ball stadium will also be
considered for future relocation outside of Bechtel Park, possibly at RIM Park, in
association with a cluster of diamonds.
The importance of managing Bechtel Park & Woodlot as a natural resource remains
critical for ensuring our environmental responsibilities and for promoting environmental
stewardship through public education and interpretive programs.
Implementation Initiatives:
 Retain the sport fields (including indoor) at Bechtel Park with the exception of fields
#5 and #6, which are recommended to be replaced at RIM Park or a not yet
determined site in West Waterloo.
 Retain the balance of Bechtel Park as a Community Park, including the planning of
enhancements to the remaining recreational assets.
 Prepare a ‘City-Wide Outdoor Sport Facility Strategy’ to review the sport facility
inventory and make recommendations for intensifying existing sport facilities to offer
the highest possible use of the facilities we have, and make recommendations for
new facilities, if required, to be added to the inventory in the future.
 Replace the programming opportunities of fields #5 and #6 within the
recommendations of the ‘City-Wide Outdoor Sport Facility Strategy’ as the highest
priority for consideration.
 Monitor the Baseball Stadium for structural condition and for program use. Consider
an alternative location for a premium ball facility to serve in place of the Bechtel
Stadium within the context of the proposed ‘Outdoor Sport Facility Strategy’. Ideally
the replacement ball facility will be in conjunction with a cluster of ball fields for
increased programming potential.
10

 Sustain the Manulife Financial Soccer & Sports Centre, through annual asset
management plan and projects.
 Commitment to the protection of our natural resources and environmental features in
a balanced and meaningful way which aligns with the City of Waterloo’s Strategic
Value of ‘Our Living Environment’.
Policy Statement #2
 Provide Cemetery Services to the Community
The City of Waterloo will continue to provide a diverse range of cemetery services for
cremation and burial choices to serve the Waterloo community.
There is an immediate need for additional traditional interment lot inventory, and the
reality is that acquisition, approvals and development of a new cemetery site is
anticipated to take several years to complete. It is recommended that a portion of
Bechtel Park be reallocated/converted to cemetery use to address short range needs,
until the new site is available.
Implementation Initiatives:
 Continue to offer cemetery services that meet varying needs of Waterloo’s culturally
diverse community.
 Continue to promote and increase opportunities for cremation services on the
Parkview Cemetery lands.
 Continue to intensify/maximize land-use for traditional interment lots.
 Engage in a process to potentially establish a new cemetery at a new location before
2025.
 Provide a supply of cemetery inventory at Parkview Cemetery, at minimum, until
opening a new cemetery.
 Expand the Parkview Cemetery lands by reallocating a maximum area of 4
hectares/10 acres of Bechtel Park lands at the location of sport fields #5 and #6.
 Plan for a seamless implementation process with no negative impact to user groups.
 Pursue partnership and collaboration with neighbouring municipalities (Kitchener or
others) for a new cemetery and future cemetery services.
 Expand lands adjacent the Catholic Section in conjunction with realignment of the
Bridge Street entrance.
 Implement a plan for the use of the North-West Cemetery area.
 Consider the opportunities for cemetery amenities, raised columbarium or crypts,
and/or other services.
 Continue development of cremation dedication and disposition options.
 Implement enhancements to create an inviting, special place of remembrance.
 Beautify north-west slope & establish a memorial tree area, including walking paths
and seating nodes.
11

 Enhance the Children’s Section as a place for reflection with seating and
meaningful artistic elements.
 Continue to include high quality architectural, sculptural and natural elements to
enhance the overall interest and character of the cemetery.
 Consider opportunities to engage the community in guided walks in the cemetery to
learn about cultural heritage and civic history.
 Explore potential for Green Burial services in the cemetery expansion, provided the
green burial policies will support intensification strategies.
Policy Statement #3
 Operate Cemeteries as Self-Funding Enterprise
 Develop strategies to sustain / operate Waterloo Cemeteries as a self-funded
enterprise model.
 Develop a strategy to fund the acquisition and development of a new cemetery
through a full cost recovery model.
 Utilize the Cemetery Reserve to implement cemetery initiatives. Develop strategies
to increase the cemetery reserve fund pr incipal balance in preparation for future
expansion.
 Allocate 100% of Cemetery Year End Surplus Revenues to the Cemetery Reserve.
 Continue to review and revise cemetery tariffs/fees/bylaws to support cemetery
operations, Care and Maintenance Funds and Reserve Funds.
 Continue to increase Care & Maintenance Fund (CMF) contributions, to ensure that
adequate funds are available to perpetually support the cemeteries.
 Continue to develop options to offset the cost of Bechtel Park overhead, which is
currently supported by Waterloo Cemeteries.
Policy Statement #4
 Enhance & Integrate the Park & Cemetery
The cemetery and park open space network is currently fragmented (by fencing) into
two separate, distinct uses. The goal is to weave land-uses together by connecting
spaces with welcoming transitions between uses. Walking paths, trees and native
vegetation will unify the lands while providing natural buffers.
Implementation Initiatives:
 Visually and Physically Connect the Park and Cemetery
12

 Design a seamless visual transition between the park and the cemetery, while
sustaining the need for some division between the two land uses.
 Connect the park, woodlot and cemetery with looping walking paths / trails to
encourage use of the whole property for leisure walking and running.
 Consider areas of shared parking for cemetery and park.
 Increase Trees and Vegetation
 Consider increasing natural landscape elements in the cemetery to merge the
natural environment and reduce operating maintenance costs.
 Establish a shaded central corridor through Bechtel Park with additional trees.
 Consider zones for ‘pockets’ of additional tree plantings.
 Consider expanding the memorial tree, stone and bench opportunities within
Parkview Cemetery to extend throughout Bechtel Park.
 Improve Access to Park & Cemetery
 Realign the entry/exit road at Bridge Street for improved access for vehicles,
pedestrians and cyclists.
 Enhance the Bridge Street entrance to create a more significant point of entry,
including signage and gateway features.
 Link the Bridge Street entrance to Parkview Cemetery to serve as a second
access/exit point to the cemetery.
 Initiate a process to explore opportunities for a signalized entry/exit to the
Parkview/Bechtel lands.
 Explore connections beyond the property edge to other trail corridors and
destinations.
 Focus on Pedestrians
 Place a greater emphasis on pedestrian access, circulation and comfort to
encourage walking.
 Install pedestrian sidewalk on University Avenue from Bridge Street to Parkview
entrance.
 Expand and enhance walking surfaces, seating nodes and climate controls (shade
trees & wind breaks).
 Install bike racks.
 Develop Trails for Walking, Running, Skiing
 Complete the trail network - introduce a pathway system that links the park
entrance to the sport facilities, the cemetery, leash free zone to the woodlot trails,
to encourage walking throughout the lands.
 Consider the needs of cross-country skiers for evening lighting.
 Consider ways to separate ski trails and walking trails (walkers degrade the
groomed ski routes).
 Sustain and consider increasing the network of paths for running
 Refine Parking Zones
 Consider completing asphalt surfacing for north lot at Indoor Complex
 Delineate/reorganize parki ng spaces in the south area to achieve parking
efficiencies.
 Protect the Natu ral Environment
 Define, manage and protect the Bechtel Park Reserve (including the woodlot,
creek, wetlands) by establishing a clear boundary and buffer zone.
13

 Consider and limit impacts to the natural habitat in all programmed and passive
activities by defining zones.
 Develop and communicate clear practices/policy to protect the lands from impacts.
 Introduce tree program for tree donations and other tree planting programs for the
north-west lands (slope) of the cemetery
Policy Statement #5:
 Seek Partnerships
Partnerships and collaboration is a predominant principle in the City of Waterloo
Strategic Plan 2007-2010. Cu ltivation of partnerships is desirable and necessary to
implement the recommended initiatives of the Master Plan.
Implementation Initiatives:
 Seek out partnership with user groups to expand indoor and outdoor facilities for;
 a shared-use community space
 expanded washroom facilities
 program spaces for outdoor education programming (Waterloo Region District
School Board Outdoor Education Program, Waterloo Region Nordic Ski Club,
camps, etc.)
 recreational facility upgrades
 gathering space/place
 Seek out partnership to review vehicular, pedestrian and cyclist circulation in the
Bridge Street and University Avenue area. Ideally this should be a collaborative
effort between the Region of Waterloo Transportation Department and Waterloo
Region District School Board, with public input support from the University Downs
Neighbourhood Association.
 Work with the City of Kitchener and potentially other neighbouring municipalities to
consider opportunities for shared cemetery services.
 Seek out partnership with user groups and community organizations to replace the
premium sport facilities (fields #5 & #6 and ball stadium) at an alternate major sport
cluster venue such as RIM Park, a proposed west side location or another location
as per the Recreation and Leisure Services Master Plan.
14

 Explore partnership opportunities with community groups to implement recreational
amenities at Bechtel Park and Parkview Cemetery that will continue to support
healthy lifestyles opportunities for Waterloo residents.
15

This concept plan illustrates the recommended land-use designations to implement the Master

4.0 Implementation Plan
The Implementation Plan establishes target timeframes for significant changes. It
provides a guideline for Council and staff to plan, fund and execute what are considered
to be major Master Plan Recommendations between 2009 and 2025.
The Implementation Strategy provides the community and key stakeholders with
timeframes for facility changes, which will provide time for consideration of program-use
modifications where necessary.
Implementation of Phase One is allocated within the current 2009-2010 capital budget
and operating budget. Note that items over $100,000 in cost will be presented to
Council for funding approval.
